Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing & procurement/security sync

Hi Ben / Elena —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation, it would be helpful to run a short multi-stakeholder session to align on the dedicated capacity sizing you’ll likely need and to cover procurement next steps and the security checklist. Proposed agenda (30–45 mins):
- Quick recap of current usage profile (Ravi)
- Redwood Dedicated sizing recommendation (Sergio)
- Procurement timeline / PO details (Elena)
- Security evidence and outstanding Qs (security@acme)
- Next steps / action owners

I attached a draft sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) and your usage forecast we received (acme-usage-forecast-2026Q3.csv) — Sergio, can you prepare two recommended configs (conservative and aggressive) with estimated monthly spend?

A few slots that work for our team (all times EDT):
- Wed 6/16, 10:00–10:45
- Thu 6/17, 14:00–14:45
- Fri 6/18, 09:30–10:15

Alternatively, feel free to pick any open slot on my Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/30min-demo

Thanks — looking to keep this tight so procurement has a clear path for signatures.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112
Redwood Inference

Thanks — I pulled the worksheet into a short recommendation. Attached: security-qna-summary.pdf (high-level answers) and a sheet with two configs:
1) Conservative: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs, target 8 concurrent requests / sustained 120k tokens/day — estimated $14k/mo (with prefix caching)
2) Aggressive: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs, target 20 concurrent requests / sustained 420k tokens/day — estimated $45k/mo (includes KV cache layer + higher concurrency)

Key assumptions are listed in the attachment. If Ravi can confirm peak concurrency and average request length we can tune the tiers. I’m happy to run the sizing portion of the call and share the spreadsheet during the meeting.

Sergio Alvarez

sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
